_README: TOPICAL TEMPLATE — Stage 2 scoped fact-build for 3 domains ABSENT from the standard facts-template.json (health/pharmacy/hospital billing, Balearic ferries, public holidays/closures). Same contract as the standard template: do NOT change field NAMES or STRUCTURE, fill VALUES only, keep every key (null if you can't fill it). Frame everything for the audience in _meta. STATUS MODEL: 'verified' = confirmed against an OFFICIAL source (URL in source_url); 'agreed_stable' = confident, no source opened; 'verify_recommended' = change-prone or high-stakes, flag it; 'serve_live' = volatile, must NOT be frozen (prices, exchange-driven costs). Return ONLY valid JSON in EXACTLY this structure. Fill EVERY section.
_fact_field_shape: Every FACT uses: { value, source_url, status (verified|agreed_stable|verify_recommended|serve_live), notes }. For 'verified' the source_url MUST be the official page you checked. Never invent a source.

health_care._note: Covers: Bringing Medication into Spain / Getting Treated in Barcelona: Pharmacy, Clinic or ER / What to Expect When a Spanish Hospital Bills You. YMYL — be conservative, prefer verify_recommended over agreed_stable.

prescription_medication_rules.value: Travelers may bring ordinary prescription medication for personal use (typically up to a 3-month supply) in original packaging with pharmacy labels showing the patient's name. Carry the original US prescription or a doctor's letter detailing diagnosis, dosage, and treatment. Spanish pharmacies cannot fill a US prescription; a local Spanish doctor must issue a new one for refills.
prescription_medication_rules.notes: quantity limits (e.g. ~personal supply for trip length), need for original packaging / doctor's letter or prescription copy

controlled_substances_note.value: Narcotics and psychotropics (opioids, ADHD stimulants such as Adderall/methylphenidate, certain benzodiazepines) require prior authorization from the Spanish Agency of Medicines and Medical Devices (AEMPS). Non-Schengen (US) travelers email estupefacientes_viajeros@aemps.es with prescription, passport copy, and flight details; authorization is limited (often to 30 days' supply even for longer trips). Adderall has no Spanish equivalent and faces stricter scrutiny. Carry original packaging and doctor's letter.
controlled_substances_note.notes: narcotics/psychotropics — Schengen certificate requirement for travelers carrying controlled meds across borders

customs_declaration_threshold.value: No fixed value threshold for personal-use medicines; quantity must match the prescribed treatment (normally ≤3 months) and not raise suspicion of trafficking. Medicines for personal use are exempt from the general traveler duty-free value limits. Declare controlled substances if asked or for larger quantities.

farmacia_identification.value: Look for the green cross (cruz verde) illuminated sign outside. Pharmacies are marked 'Farmacia'.

farmacia_de_guardia.value: Rotating 24-hour duty pharmacies cover nights, Sundays, and holidays. Every closed pharmacy posts the address of the nearest on-duty one. In Barcelona use the official live finder Farmaguia (farmaguia.net) from the Col·legi de Farmacèutics de Barcelona or the 061 CatSalut Respon app; Google Maps is unreliable for the rotation.
farmacia_de_guardia.notes: 24h rotating duty-pharmacy system — how a tourist finds the open one

otc_vs_prescription_differences.value: Virtually all medicines are sold only in pharmacies (not supermarkets). Paracetamol 1 g and ibuprofen 400 mg are OTC; ibuprofen 600 mg, codeine combinations, and many antibiotics require a Spanish prescription. Metamizol (Nolotil) is a common OTC-level painkiller in Spain but not available in the US. High-dose melatonin (>1.9-2 mg) is prescription-only in Spain. Emergency contraception is OTC. Pharmacists will not fill a US script.
otc_vs_prescription_differences.notes: things OTC in Spain but Rx-only in the US or vice versa

pharmacist_role.value: Spanish pharmacists are highly trained and routinely assess and advise on minor ailments (colds, mild pain, digestive issues, skin problems) without a doctor visit. Describe symptoms; they recommend and dispense appropriate OTC products and will direct you to a doctor when needed.
pharmacist_role.notes: Spanish pharmacists routinely advise/treat minor ailments directly

private_clinic_access.value: Walk-in private clinics and tourist-oriented medical centers are widely available in Barcelona. Typical GP/consultation fees roughly €60-150; expect higher for specialists or after-hours. Many accept cards and speak English. Useful for non-emergencies to avoid public ER waits.
private_clinic_access.notes: walk-in private clinics for tourists — typical cost range

public_hospital_er_access.value: Anyone can walk into Urgencias (public hospital ER) and will be triaged by severity. Non-EU/US tourists are treated but later billed. Insurance card is not required at the door for emergency care; treatment is provided first. Waiting times for non-urgent cases can be several hours, especially in peak season.
public_hospital_er_access.notes: urgencias access for non-residents, triage-based, whether insurance card is asked for AT the door

when_to_choose_which.value: Minor ailments (cold, mild GI upset, simple rash, refill advice) -> pharmacy first. Non-emergency but needs a doctor (infection needing antibiotics, minor injury, ongoing symptoms) -> private clinic for speed and English. True emergency (chest pain, severe trauma, difficulty breathing, major accident) -> call 112 or go straight to public Urgencias. 112 operators speak English.

billing_model_public.value: Public hospitals treat emergencies regardless of insurance status. Non-EU tourists (Americans) are usually billed afterward; the invoice may be handed at discharge or mailed later. Some facilities use intermediaries that can inflate the final amount charged to the patient. Keep all paperwork.
billing_model_public.notes: does a public hospital bill a non-EU tourist directly, and when — at discharge or by mail

billing_model_private.value: Private clinics and hospitals typically require payment or a credit-card guarantee upfront or at the time of service. They issue itemized invoices suitable for US insurance claims.

typical_costs.value: Rough ranges only (volatile, serve live): basic public ER visit for non-EU tourist often €100-300; with tests/imaging higher. Overnight ward stay hundreds of euros per night; ICU significantly more. Private GP visit €60-150. Ambulance costs extra. Never treat these as fixed prices.
typical_costs.notes: rough ranges only: ER visit, ambulance ride, one overnight stay — never frozen as durable prices

travel_insurance_necessity.value: Strongly recommended and practically essential for Americans. Medicare/Medicaid do not cover care abroad. Without insurance you pay out-of-pocket and seek reimbursement later (or not). Travel medical insurance with evacuation coverage is the practical requirement for this audience.

what_to_keep_for_reimbursement.value: Itemized invoice (factura), medical report (informe médico), discharge summary, prescriptions, and all payment receipts. Request English or Spanish originals before leaving the facility; US insurers need clear documentation of diagnosis, treatment, and amounts paid.
what_to_keep_for_reimbursement.notes: itemized invoice / informe médico / payment receipts for a US insurer claim

ferries_balearics._note: Covers: Ferries from Barcelona to the Balearics: Fast vs Slow / When a Balearic Ferry Cancels, and What You're Owed.

operators.notes: e.g. Trasmediterránea, Baleària — who actually runs Barcelona-Balearics

port_terminal.value: Port de Barcelona has multiple ferry terminals (F1 / Moll Adossat / Lepant for many Baleària sailings; F2 / Moll de Sant Bertran for Trasmed and GNV; others for additional operators). Confirm exact terminal on your ticket. Reachable by metro (Drassanes L3 for some Baleària points; Paral·lel for others), bus, or taxi (roughly 10-20 min from central areas). Allow extra time for check-in, especially with a vehicle.
port_terminal.notes: which Port de Barcelona terminal, how to get there from the center

to_palma_mallorca.value: Fast ferry (Baleària Margarita Salas and similar) ~3.5 hours; conventional overnight ferries ~7-8.5 hours. Foot-passenger prices often start in the low tens of euros off-peak and rise substantially in summer or for cabins/vehicles — check live.
to_palma_mallorca.notes: fast vs slow ferry duration + rough price range

to_ibiza.value: Mostly overnight conventional ferries ~8-9.5 hours. Multiple daily options in high season from Baleària, Trasmed, GNV. Prices volatile; book ahead in summer.

to_menorca.value: Direct services to Ciutadella or Maó; fast options ~3.5-5.5 hours, conventional overnight ~7-9 hours. Seasonality is strong — more frequent in summer. Some routings may involve other ports; confirm direct status on booking.
to_menorca.notes: note if it's direct or routed via Mallorca/Valencia, and seasonality

fast_vs_slow_tradeoffs.value: Fast ferry: saves a full day, higher price, more motion in rough seas, limited cabin options. Conventional overnight: cheaper base fare, cabins available for sleep, arrives early morning, better for cars or budget travelers who value rest. Choose fast if time-sensitive and traveling light; choose slow/overnight for comfort, cost, or vehicle.

booking_advice.value: In peak summer book weeks to months ahead, especially for cabins or car spaces. Foot passengers have more last-minute flexibility. Prefer the operator's own site (balearia.com, trasmed.com, gnv.it) over pure aggregators for clearest terms and changes. Check terminal and boarding instructions on the ticket.
booking_advice.notes: how far ahead in summer, walk-on vs car ferry, aggregator vs operator site

typical_causes.value: Primarily adverse weather (strong wind, high seas) that exceeds safe operating limits for the vessel type. Operational or technical issues less common but possible.

passenger_rights.value: EU Regulation 1177/2010 applies. If cancelled or delayed >90 minutes at departure: choice of full refund (within 7 days) or re-routing at no extra cost under comparable conditions. Care obligations (meals, refreshments, possibly accommodation) apply while waiting. Compensation (25% or 50% of the ticket price) may be due for significant arrival delays depending on scheduled duration; exceptions exist for extraordinary circumstances such as weather.
passenger_rights.notes: EU ferry passenger rights regulation — compensation, rerouting, care obligations

operator_rebooking_practice.value: Operators typically offer rebooking on the next available sailing or a refund. Practices vary; contact the carrier promptly and keep records of all communications and original tickets.

travel_insurance_interaction.value: Standard travel insurance often covers additional costs from a cancelled ferry (missed connections, extra accommodation, alternative transport) if the cancellation is outside your control, subject to policy wording and exclusions. Check your policy for 'transport disruption' or 'trip interruption' coverage; pure weather cancellations are frequently covered while operator insolvency may not be.

public_holidays_closures._note: Covers: What Closes on a Spanish Public Holiday (and feeds the existing barcelona-august-shutdown article as a targeted addition). Dates are change-prone per year — flag accordingly.

value.name: National Day of Spain (Fiesta Nacional / Hispanidad)
Saint Stephen's Day / Boxing Day (Sant Esteve)
Whit Monday / Pentecost Monday (Segona Pasqua / Lunes de Pascua Granada)
La Mercè (Mare de Déu de la Mercè)

barcelona_local_holidays.notes: [{name, typical_date}] — city-specific (e.g. La Mercè, Santa Eulàlia)

what_typically_closes.value: Banks, government offices, and most small independent shops close. Large chains and tourist-zone shops may open limited hours (especially in designated tourist shopping zones). Many restaurants in residential neighborhoods close or run reduced service; tourist-area restaurants, bars, and cafés usually stay open. Museums and attractions often follow holiday hours or close — check individually. Public transit runs on a reduced 'horario festivo' (holiday schedule). Pharmacies operate via the rotating guardia system.
what_typically_closes.notes: shops (small vs chain), restaurants, banks, museums, transit schedule ('horario festivo')

august_shutdown_specifics.value: Many family-run neighborhood shops, bakeries, and local restaurants close for 1-3 weeks in August (especially around the 15th) while owners vacation. Tourist-core areas (Gothic Quarter, Born, Barceloneta, Rambla) and major chains/malls largely stay open. Supermarkets and essential services continue; some on reduced hours. Public services and museums generally operate, though staff may be thinner. The national holiday on 15 August amplifies closures.
august_shutdown_specifics.notes: how widespread, typical closure window, what stays open (malls, tourist-facing restaurants, museums) — feeds barcelona-august-shutdown

advance_planning_note.value: Around major holidays and in mid-August, book popular restaurants and check attraction opening hours in advance. Confirm ferry and train schedules, as some services reduce frequency. For pharmacies use the official guardia finder rather than assuming normal hours. Carry cash or cards, as some small places that remain open may have limited banking access.

_open_questions._note: Anything genuinely unsure / conflicting / needing a real source. Be honest.
value: Exact current AEMPS processing times and whether a 30-day limit is strictly enforced for all controlled substances for non-Schengen travelers (sources vary slightly between 30 days and up to 3 months).

Precise typical public-hospital ER invoice amounts for non-EU tourists in Barcelona after any intermediary mark-ups; published ranges exist but actual bills vary widely and some older reports note significant inflation by billing agents.
Whether every public hospital in Catalonia consistently mails bills versus requiring on-the-spot payment for non-residents without Spanish address.
Exact 2027 local holiday dates for Barcelona (city council chooses two local days each year; 2026 ones are confirmed but future years need annual verification).
Current vehicle and cabin pricing volatility on Balearic routes — too fluid for any durable figure beyond 'check live'.
